patterns: how do you say cheap in tagalog
entries.answer: Mura means cheap, and in everyday use it is nearly always about price rather than quality. Saying a thing is mura is not the same as saying it is bad, though sellers sometimes use it that way. Careful with the opposite, because mura can also mean gentle or soft in other contexts.

patterns: what is the opposite of kulang
entries.answer: Kulang means lacking or insufficient, and it is the word you reach for when something is not enough. It applies to a budget that will not cover the bills, to sleep that was too short, and to a skill you have not built yet. Its opposite is sobra, which means excess rather than sufficiency, so saying hindi kulang is not quite the same as saying sobra.

entries.answer: Sobra means excess or too much, and it describes having more than is needed rather than having a lot. Too much sugar is sobra ang asin, and someone who is being unreasonable is sobra na. The paired word is kulang for not enough, and Filipino treats these as the two ends of the same scale.

patterns: how do you say good in tagalog
entries.answer: Maganda means good, nice or beautiful, and it covers all three because Filipino does not separate them the way English does. It describes weather, food, a person and an idea without changing form. The opposite is hindi maganda or masama for something bad, and note that masama is stronger, closer to evil or serious.

patterns: how do you say bad in tagalog
entries.answer: Masama means bad or wrong, and it is a strong word that leans towards evil or serious rather than a mild negative. A small mistake is hindi maganda rather than masama. It is also the word used for a person behaving badly, so describing someone as masama carries real judgement rather than a description.

patterns: how do you say big in tagalog
entries.answer: Malaki means big or large, and it is used for physical size, for quantities and for importance. A big favour is malaki ang tulong, and a large city is malaki ang lungsod. The opposite is maliit, and the same word also means a lot, so malaking pabor is both a big and a great favour.

patterns: how do you say small in tagalog
entries.answer: Maliit means small, and it is the everyday word for physical size and for quantity. It is the direct opposite of malaki, and unlike some size words in English it has no second meaning, so it cannot be misread in a sentence. Maliit na lang means only small, which is often a way of minimising something.

entries.answer: Bago means new, and it is the ordinary adjective for something made recently, and also the ordinary adverb for recently, which is the same word doing two jobs. A thing that is bago is recently made or recently acquired, so a bago ng katay, a new car, and it takes a marker when the thing is named, as in bagong-bago for something that has just come. The recent sense covers an action rather than an object, so bago lang ako kumain means I have just eaten, and a learner coming from English often reaches for the separate English pair new and recently and is surprised one word covers both. A common alternative in the Philippines is the borrowed term bago from the English brand for instant noodles, which is a different sense entirely: a bago is the noodle dish, not a new thing, so the word genuinely has three unrelated meanings in ordinary use.
